Topic 01 — Regulation & Classification

Drug vs. Dietary Supplement

Drug (FDA)
Changes body structure/function.
Includes anything that stimulates hormone secretion.
Requires FDA approval for safety + effectiveness before sale.
Dietary Supplement (DSHEA 1994)
Contains a vitamin, mineral, herb, amino acid, or metabolite/extract of one.
Must be labeled "dietary supplement." No FDA pre-approval required.
Photo: Towfiqu barbhuiya / Unsplash
Topic 01 — Regulation & Classification

Who Writes the Banned Lists

  • GlobalWADA — sets the banned list for the IOC + affiliated national agencies (USADA, UKAD, SIA)
  • US CollegeNCAA — publishes its own annual banned substances list, updated yearly
  • Pro LeaguesMLB, NFL, NHL, MLS each maintain independent banned-substance policies
No single, complete banned list exists. Every sport's governing body publishes its own.
Topic 01 — Regulation & Classification

The 8 Banned Categories

CategoryExamples
Anabolic AgentsAAS, testosterone precursors, SARMs
Hormone/Metabolic ModulatorsAromatase inhibitors, SERMs, anti-estrogens
Beta-2 AgonistsAlbuterol, salbutamol, salmeterol
Diuretics/Masking AgentsUsed to conceal other banned substances
NarcoticsFentanyl, morphine, oxycodone, tramadol
Peptide Hormones/Growth FactorshGH, hCG, EPO, IGF-1
StimulantsAmphetamines and related compounds
Topic 01 — Regulation & Classification

The Contamination Risk

1
Undeclared compounds found in dietary supplement products
2
Chemical analysis of 44 online "SARM" products → only 52% actually contained a SARM
3
39% contained a completely different, undisclosed drug

An athlete can test positive without knowingly taking a banned substance. Third-party testing and reputable brands matter.

Topic 02

Anabolic-

Steroids

Topic 02 — Anabolic-Androgenic Steroids

What They Are + Administration

Oral
Methandrostenolone, oxandrolone, stanozolol.
Athletes report doses up to 300 mg/day vs.
15 mg/day clinical replacement.
Injectable
Testosterone esters — more potent, avoid first-pass liver metabolism.
Half-life ranges 1.5 days (propionate)
→ 3 months (buciclate).
Transdermal
Creams, gels, patches.
Increasingly common for medical use; less common for athletic doping.
Photo: Олег Мороз / Unsplash
Topic 02 — Anabolic-Androgenic Steroids

Dosing Patterns

1
Stacking → multiple drugs simultaneously for additive potency (efficacy unproven)
2
Cycling → weeks/months on, alternated with off periods
3
Pyramiding → dose steadily ↑ then "steps down" toward cycle end
4
Typical regimen: 3.1 agents avg, 5–10 wk cycles, 5–29× physiologic replacement dose
Forbes: total steroid dose has a logarithmic relationship to lean mass gain — low doses = slight effect, larger doses = progressively greater gain.
Topic 02 — Anabolic-Androgenic Steroids

Efficacy — Muscle & Strength

Mechanism
Supraphysiologic doses
↑ muscle protein synthesis
→ ↑ lean body mass, even without training.
Case Study
Bodybuilder, 53 mg/day for 1 yr
→ +7 kg (15 lb) fat-free mass, +11% vastus lateralis fiber area in 6 months.
Same case: after withdrawal → atrophic testicles, ↓ LH/FSH/testosterone, ↓ HDL cholesterol.
Topic 02 — Anabolic-Androgenic Steroids

Efficacy — Performance & Psychology

Athletic Performance
Benefits realized at supraphysiologic doses, degree varies by training status.
Psychological
~60% of users report
↑ irritability + aggressiveness.
Mood swings, psychotic episodes reported.
Pope et al.: significant ↑ aggressiveness + manic scores after 12 wk testosterone cypionate — effect not uniform across individuals.
Topic 02 — Anabolic-Androgenic Steroids

Adverse Effects by System

SystemEffects
Cardiovascular↑ BP, lipid changes, ↓ myocardial function
Endocrine/GenitourinaryGynecomastia, ↓ sperm count, testicular atrophy
FemalesMenstrual irregularity, clitoromegaly, deepened voice
DermatologicalAcne, male pattern baldness
Hepatic↑ liver tumor + damage risk
MusculoskeletalPremature epiphyseal closure, tendon tears
PsychologicalMania, depression, aggression, mood swings
Topic 02 — Anabolic-Androgenic Steroids

Who Uses Steroids?

1
Est. 2.9–4.0 million Americans have used AAS in their lifetime
2
~7% of male US high school seniors report use
3
1/3 of teen users not in school sports — main reason: appearance, not performance
4
"Muscle dysmorphia" (reverse anorexia) linked to most severe steroid-related illness, mainly in bodybuilders
Topic 02 — Recap

Anabolic Steroids — Recap

✅
Efficacy
↑ MPS + lean mass at supraphysiologic doses — dose-response is logarithmic, not linear.
✅
Dosing
Stacking, cycling, pyramiding — no proven added efficacy from stacking.
✅
Adverse Effects
Cardiovascular, endocrine, hepatic, psychological risks — often underreported by users.
Topic 03

Precursors, SARMs

Topic 03 — Precursors, SARMs & Peptides

Prohormones — Testosterone Precursors

The Theory
Androstenedione, androstenediol, DHEA
→ theorized to
↑ testosterone, strength, muscle size.
The Reality
Only 1/5 (andro) to 1/10 (DHEA) the biological activity of testosterone.
Controlled trials: no significant strength/mass gains.
Andro Project conclusion: no training benefit, but ↑ estrogen-related compounds + unfavorable lipid/cardiac risk profile.
Photo: Anirudh / Unsplash
Topic 03 — Precursors, SARMs & Peptides

SARMs — Selective Androgen Receptor Modulators

Mechanism
Tissue-selective AR agonists — target muscle/bone, spare liver/prostate.
No FDA-approved SARM exists; all investigational.
Popular Compounds
Ostarine (MK-2866), Ligandrol (LGD-4033), Testolone (RAD140), Andarine, Myanabol (YK-11).
WADA prohibits all SARMs at all times, in and out of competition.
Topic 03 — Precursors, SARMs & Peptides

SARM Safety & Efficacy

1
3 wk LGD-4033 → dose-dependent ↑ lean mass, alongside ↓ testosterone, SHBG, HDL-C
2
Short-term use well tolerated, but consistent ↓ HDL-C + ↑ liver enzymes
3
Case reports: acute myocarditis + liver injury with RAD140 in recreational users
FDA warning: SARMs linked to heart attack/stroke risk, liver injury, sleep disturbance, sexual dysfunction, miscarriage.
Topic 03 — Precursors, SARMs & Peptides

Peptides — The Emerging Frontier

GH Secretagogues
MK-677: early promise for bone/fat-free mass in older adults — trials halted,
↑ congestive heart failure risk.
GLP-1 Agonists
Liraglutide, semaglutide — strong weight-loss efficacy in obesity, no evidence of benefit without excess body fat.
Topic 03 — Precursors, SARMs & Peptides

WADA-Banned Peptide Classes

ClassExamples
GonadotropinshCG, LH, GnRH + agonists
Growth Hormone ReleasersGHRH, sermorelin, hexarelin, MK-677
Growth FactorsIGF-1, FGFs, HGF, PDGF
EPO-RelatedEPO, EPO-mimetics, HIF activators
Topic 03 — Recap

Precursors, SARMs & Peptides — Recap

✅
Prohormones
Weak biological activity, no proven training benefit — legally controlled since 2004.
✅
SARMs
Promising lean-mass signal, but real cardiac/hepatic risk. Zero FDA-approved products.
✅
Peptides
Rapidly evolving category — WADA-banned classes are broad and explicit.
Topic 04

HCG, Insulin,
HGH & EPO

Topic 04 — HCG, Insulin, HGH & EPO

HCG — Human Chorionic Gonadotropin

Mechanism
Mimics luteinizing hormone
→ stimulates Leydig cells
→ testosterone can nearly double within 4 days.
Why Athletes Use It
Restarts endogenous testosterone production suppressed at the end of a steroid cycle.
No performance-enhancing value for females. Minimal documented adverse effects — mainly injection-site pain/swelling.
Photo: Mykenzie Johnson / Unsplash
Topic 04 — HCG, Insulin, HGH & EPO

Insulin — The Anabolic Hormone

Mechanism
↑ glucose + amino acid uptake into cells
→ ↑ protein synthesis,
↓ protein breakdown.
The Danger
Exogenous injection by bodybuilders (chasing GH/IGF-1 synergy) risks immediate death or coma from severe hypoglycemia.
Topic 04 — HCG, Insulin, HGH & EPO

HGH — Human Growth Hormone

1
Anabolic: stimulates bone/muscle growth, ↑ glucose/amino acid uptake, mobilizes fatty acids
2
No studies confirm ergogenic efficacy in professional athletes
3
Athlete doses far exceed clinical replacement — undetectable in urine (blood test since 2004 Olympics)
4
Adverse: gigantism (pre-puberty), acromegaly (post-puberty) — disfiguring, irreversible
Topic 04 — HCG, Insulin, HGH & EPO

EPO — Blood Doping

Autologous
Transfusion of one's own stored blood.
Homologous
Transfusion from a matched donor.
Recombinant EPO
Most common method since late 1980s — stimulates kidney production of new RBCs.
Topic 04 — HCG, Insulin, HGH & EPO

EPO — Efficacy vs. Risk

Efficacy
↑ Hgb 5–17%, Hct 8–19%
→ ↑ aerobic capacity/power 7–10%, time-to-exhaustion +9–50%.
Risk
↑ blood viscosity
→ clotting, stroke, cardiac/pulmonary embolism.
Dehydration compounds risk during endurance events.
Lance Armstrong admitted EPO use across his cycling career. Multiple competitive cyclist deaths linked to EPO administration.
Reference: Lance Armstrong doping case / Wikipedia
Topic 04 — Recap

HCG, Insulin, HGH & EPO — Recap

✅
HCG
Restarts endogenous T post-cycle — low documented risk.
✅
Insulin
Anabolic mechanism, but exogenous use risks fatal hypoglycemia.
✅
HGH
Unproven athletic efficacy, real risk of acromegaly at ergogenic doses.
✅
EPO
Proven aerobic benefit, but among the most dangerous ergogenic aids — linked to athlete deaths.
Topic 05

Beta-Agonists &
Beta-Blockers

Topic 05 — Beta-Agonists & Beta-Blockers

Beta-Agonists — Clenbuterol

Mechanism
Chemically related to epinephrine.
↑ lean mass +
↓ fat — a "partitioning agent."
Dosing Pattern
2× clinical dose, cyclic: 3 wk on/3 wk off, with 2 days on/2 days off during "on" weeks.
Evidence base is thin — mostly from heart-failure and muscle-wasting patients, not healthy athletes. Adverse: tachycardia, tremors, insomnia.
Topic 05 — Beta-Agonists & Beta-Blockers

Beta-Blockers — Precision Sports

Mechanism
Blocks β-adrenergic receptors
→ ↓ anxiety + tremor.
Benefits archers, marksmen, shooters.
Dose-Response
Higher-dose oxprenolol (80mg vs 40mg)
→ greater shooting accuracy.
Ergolytic for endurance: ↓ max HR, ↓ VO2, ↓ 10km race time. Risks: bronchospasm, heart block, bradycardia.
Image by Pexels from Pixabay
Topic 05 — Beta-Agonists & Beta-Blockers

What Alcohol Does to Recovery

1
~6.3 standard drinks post-exercise → worsens eccentric-induced strength loss
2
High-dose alcohol → ↓ mTORC1 signaling → ↓ muscle protein synthesis (most pronounced in men)
3
Diuretic effect: ~10 mL excess urine per gram ethanol ingested
4
Binge drinking (4–5 drinks/2 hr) → disrupts sleep quality + next-day BP regulation
Topic 05 — Recap

Beta-Agonists, Beta-Blockers & Alcohol — Recap

✅
Beta-Agonists
Partitioning effect claimed, but human evidence thin — real cardiac side effects.
✅
Beta-Blockers
Genuinely effective for precision sports, but ergolytic for endurance performance.
✅
Alcohol
Impairs strength recovery, MPS, and sleep — dose-dependent, most harmful post-training.

Amino Acid

Topic 06 — Amino Acid Supplements

EAA & BCAA — The Leucine Trigger

The Finding
Only EAAs (not nonessential AAs) needed to stimulate MPS.
Of the 3 BCAAs, leucine is the key driver via Akt/mTOR.
The Timing
6g EAA + sugar 30 min pre-training
→ 158% greater anabolic response vs.
same dose post-training.
Leucine intake→Akt/mTOR pathway→↑ Muscle protein synthesis
Photo: Andrey Khoviakov / Unsplash
Topic 06 — Amino Acid Supplements

Arginine — Claims vs. Reality

The Claim
↑ nitric oxide
→ vasodilation
→ ↑ muscle blood flow
→ ↑ endurance performance.
The Evidence
Does not raise NO beyond exercise-alone levels, does not
↑ blood flow, does not improve endurance in healthy adults.
Well tolerated up to 13g. GI distress (nausea, cramps, diarrhea) at 13–30g doses.
Topic 06 — Amino Acid Supplements

HMB — β-Hydroxy-β-Methylbutyrate

Mechanism
Leucine metabolite.
↓ protein breakdown by inhibiting the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway.
Who Benefits
Untrained beginners + trained athletes on a high-intensity, high-volume program.
Little effect if training stimulus is unchanged.
Typical dose: 3g/day, often split. No known adverse effects at standard dosing.
Topic 06 — Recap

Amino Acid Supplements — Recap

✅
EAA/BCAA
Leucine drives MPS via Akt/mTOR — timing before training amplifies the effect.
✅
Arginine
Evidence does not support NO, blood flow, or endurance claims in healthy adults.
✅
HMB
Effective anti-catabolic aid — but only with an adequate training stimulus.

Nutritional

Topic 07 — Nutritional Muscle Buffers

Muscle Buffering Capacity (MBC)

H⁺ accumulation→↓ intramuscular pH→↓ high-intensity performance
Strong positive relationship between MBC and repeated-sprint ability, anaerobic threshold, and training volume — seen in basketball, soccer, rowing, cycling, sprinting.
Topic 07 — Nutritional Muscle Buffers

Beta-Alanine — Carnosine Synthesis

Mechanism
Rate-limiting substrate for carnosine — contributes up to 40% of skeletal MBC.
Dosing
2.4–6.4 g/day, split into 2–4 doses.
4 wk
→ +64% muscle carnosine.
Best for exercise >60 sec at high intensity. Only adverse effect: paresthesia (tingling) — resolves within ~1 hr, avoided with smaller split doses.
Topic 07 — Nutritional Muscle Buffers

Sodium Bicarbonate

Protocol
0.3–0.5 g/kg body mass, 60–180 min before exercise.
Best for 60 sec–6 min high-intensity efforts.
Trade-off
Doses above 0.3 g/kg
→ diarrhea, cramping, nausea, vomiting.
Test in practice, not competition.
Topic 07 — Nutritional Muscle Buffers

Sodium Citrate — The Gentler Option

BufferDoseGI Tolerability
β-Alanine2.4–6.4 g/day (split)High — only paresthesia
Sodium Bicarbonate0.3–0.5 g/kg, 60–180 min preLow above 0.3 g/kg
Sodium Citrate0.2–0.6 g/kg, 60–90 min preModerate — milder than bicarb
Topic 08

L-Carnitine

Topic 08 — L-Carnitine

Mechanism & Efficacy Reality Check

Mechanism
Transports fatty acids from cytosol into mitochondria for oxidation.
The Reality
Most studies fail to show
↑ muscle carnitine content from oral supplementation — inconsistent fat-loss evidence.
Where it does show promise: recovery. ↓ soreness/muscle damage, ↓ metabolic stress markers after high-intensity resistance exercise.
Photo: Supliful - Supplements On Demand / Unsplash
Topic 08 — L-Carnitine

Adverse Effects & Takeaway

1
2 g/day × 3 wk → ↑ androgen receptor content, ↑ IGF binding proteins
2
Up to 3 g/day × 3 wk well tolerated — no adverse hematological/metabolic events
3
Long-term/higher-dose safety data limited — don't extrapolate

Not a fat-loss supplement in practice. Best-supported role is post-exercise recovery, not lipid oxidation.

Topic 09

Creatine

Topic 09 — Creatine

Why Creatine Matters to Exercise

Muscle CP stores→Rephosphorylate ADP → ATP→Sustain high-intensity output
6-sec max effort → CP ↓ 35–57%. 30-sec max effort → CP ↓ 64–80%. CP depletion is the primary fatigue mechanism in short, intense bouts.
Photo: Alex Saks / Unsplash
Topic 09 — Creatine

Supplementation Protocol

Loading
20–25 g/day (or 0.3 g/kg) for 5 days
→ saturates muscle stores in ~5 days.
Maintenance
2 g/day (0.03 g/kg) sustains elevated levels indefinitely.
No Loading
Same saturation reached without loading — just takes ~30 days instead of 5.
Saturation ceiling: 150–160 mmol/kg dry muscle weight — more supplementation beyond this adds nothing. Levels return to baseline ~4 wk after stopping.
Topic 09 — Creatine

Efficacy — What the Evidence Shows

1
Strength gains (bench, squat, power clean) 2–3× greater vs. placebo in trained athletes
2
5-day loading alone doesn't improve single-bout sprint performance — needs 28–84 days for jump/power gains
3
Best framed as a training enhancer (less fatigue, better workout quality) rather than a direct performance drug
Topic 09 — Creatine

Body Mass & Adverse Effects — Myths vs. Facts

ClaimEvidence
Causes dehydrationNot supported by controlled studies
Causes crampingNot supported by controlled studies
Damages kidneysNo renal dysfunction in 5-day to 5-year studies
↑ body massTrue — 0.5–1.8 kg gain, mostly water + fat-free mass

Creatine is safe, inexpensive, and no supplement has stronger research support for strength, power, and lean mass.

Topic 10

Stimulants

Topic 10 — Stimulants

Caffeine — The Universal Ergogenic Aid

Dosing
3–9 mg/kg, ~60 min pre-exercise.
No added benefit above 9 mg/kg.
Aerobic Effect
Landmark study: time-to-exhaustion 75 min (placebo)
→ 96 min (caffeine) at 80% VO2max.
Adverse: anxiety, GI upset, insomnia, arrhythmias — physically addictive. Lethal dose ≈ 5g (~42 cups of coffee or 25 × 200mg tablets).
Photo: Nathan Dumlao / Unsplash
Topic 10 — Stimulants

Preworkout Energy Drinks

Standard Dose
~2 mg/kg caffeine, 60 min pre — below the 3–9 mg/kg ergogenic threshold, yet still effective.
What They Improve
Resistance training volume + some aerobic performance.
Not effective for Wingate/speed-agility tasks.
Synergy between ingredients (taurine, guarana, B vitamins) may explain benefit beyond caffeine dose alone.
Topic 10 — Stimulants

Ephedrine — Banned Since 2004

1
Effective for aerobic endurance only when combined with caffeine
2
5 mg/kg caffeine + 1 mg/kg ephedrine → 25% of subjects report vomiting/nausea
3
Lower dose (4 mg/kg caffeine + 0.8 mg/kg ephedrine) → same benefit, no side effects
4
FDA banned all ephedra products in 2004 — Rand Institute linked it to 16,000 adverse events
Topic 10 — Stimulants

Citrus Aurantium — Bitter Orange

Mechanism
Synephrine stimulates β-3 receptors
→ lipolysis, without the typical adrenergic cardiovascular effect.
The Catch
Combined with other herbals
→ ↑ systolic BP.
Currently on the NCAA banned list.
Insufficient standalone data to recommend as a performance-enhancing supplement.
Topic 10 — Stimulants

Ergogenic vs. Non-Ergogenic — Summary

SupplementVerdict
CreatineStrongly effective — strength, power, lean mass
CaffeineEffective for endurance; less clear for sprint/power
β-AlanineEffective for repeated high-intensity efforts >60 sec
HMBEffective with adequate training stimulus
Sodium BicarbonateEffective but GI side effects limit use
ArginineNot effective in healthy individuals
Topic 10 — Recap

Chapter 12 — Key Takeaway

The S&C professional's job isn't to ban conversation about ergogenic aids — it's to give athletes accurate, current, evidence-based guidance so they can make legal, safe, and informed choices.
